Four conditions force `opts.sort = true` without `--sort`, all in `src/main.zig`:

- **`--exec`**: `if (opts.exec_cmd != null and !opts.sort) opts.sort = true;` (src/main.zig:2190). It needs to know which files matched, and only the ordered path keeps that (src/main.zig:2186-2189).
- **`--heading`**: `if (opts.heading and !opts.sort) opts.sort = true;` (src/main.zig:2195). Streaming would interleave groups across files (src/main.zig:2191-2194).
- **`--pre`**: `if (opts.pre_cmd != null and !opts.sort)` sets sort (src/main.zig:2196-2197).
- **Several explicit file operands** (no directories): `if (valid_operands.items.len > 1 and all_files) opts.sort = true;` (src/main.zig:2362). This gives GNU grep argument order (src/main.zig:2357-2361).

Also, `--queries-file` batches run each query with `--json --sort` (src/main.zig:1892, 1925).

The context was truncated, so other triggers may exist.
